claims.text: Clearance revenues: taxes Israel collects for the PA under the 1994 Paris Protocol (tariffs, purchase tax, import VAT); about two-thirds of PA public revenue; past suspensions 2006, Dec 2012 (UN status), 2015 (ICC); deductions for prisoner payments since 2019 totalled NIS 3.54bn to July 2024.

2 Jul 2018 Knesset law, 87–15, deducts from clearance revenues the amount the PA pays prisoners and families of those killed; Israel says payments encourage violence; stipends ~$330m, ~35,000 families; Ashrawi called it 'highway robbery'.

After 7 Oct 2023 the security cabinet withheld the share for Gaza to prevent payments reaching Hamas; Norway arrangement Feb 2024 held that share; Norway's PM: funds 'necessary to ensure that the Palestinian Authority does not collapse'; clearance ~65% of PA income.

MAS June 2026: Israel has withheld all clearance transfers since June 2025; NIS 11.7bn withheld plus NIS 12.5bn deductions Jan 2021–Mar 2026 (44% of net clearance revenue); PA paid 50% of Feb 2026 salaries in June; debt plus arrears ~$12.4bn, 72% of 2025 GDP.

World Bank 2013: access to Area C could add $3.4bn a year, 35% of 2011 GDP, and halve the PA deficit; Israel's Foreign Ministry: issues for negotiations, Palestinian development in Israel's interest, 300+ projects approved in Area C.

UN business database update 26 Sep 2025: 158 businesses from 11 countries (most Israeli; also US, UK, Germany, France, Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, Luxembourg, Canada, China); activities include supplying settlement construction, demolitions, surveillance, natural resources.
Haaretz (2015): ~50 US tax-exempt organizations raised $281m 2009–13, $224m transferred to settlements; uses included property, and support for families of convicted Jewish terrorists (Honenu).

Peace Now July 2026: NIS 335.4m budget amendment for Settlements Ministry; NIS 294.5m defence emergency funds for settlements; NIS 103m to farms and outposts for 'security components' 2023–25; NIS 550m security roads 2026–27; >220km roads opened 2024–25.

10 Jun 2025: hours after Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK and Norway sanctioned Smotrich and Ben-Gvir for incitement, Smotrich ordered the bank indemnity cancelled, citing the PA's 'delegitimisation campaign against the State of Israel internationally'.
